insider_note: Once the numerator is rewritten as A·(derivative of the denominator) + B·(the denominator itself), the integral splits into a plain log term and a plain x term — no trig substitution is ever needed for this family of questions.

steps.label: Write the numerator as A·Dr′ + B·Dr and equate coefficients
steps.why: Any linear combination a·cosx+b·sinx can be rewritten in terms of the denominator and its OWN derivative, because {cosx, sinx} and {Dr, Dr′} both span the same 2-dimensional space of expressions — that is what makes A and B always solvable.
common_mistakes: Differentiating the denominator incorrectly, e.g. writing d/dx(4sinx+5cosx) = 4cosx+5sinx (sign slip on the second term).
Matching cosx on the LHS to sinx on the RHS by reading the equation too quickly.
steps.memory_tip: Denominator's own derivative, times A, plus the denominator itself, times B — that pair always reproduces any a·cosx+b·sinx numerator.

steps.label: Solve the pair of equations for A and B
steps.why: Eliminating B by matching its coefficient in both equations (multiplying to make both 20B) isolates A first; B then drops out from a single back-substitution.
common_mistakes: Eliminating the wrong variable, which needs an extra unnecessary step.
steps.memory_tip: Multiply each equation to match one letter's coefficient, subtract to kill it, then back-substitute for the other.

steps.label: Substitute back and split the integral
steps.why: With A and B both known numbers, the original integral splits into exactly two recognisable pieces: an f′(x)/f(x) form (a pure log) and a plain constant.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to substitute the found values of A and B back into (i) before splitting the integral.
Splitting the integral before finding A and B, which leaves unknowns in the working.
steps.memory_tip: Once A and B are numbers, the integral is ALWAYS a log plus a plain x term — no other outcome is possible for this family.

steps.label: Integrate both parts for the final answer
steps.why: ∫f′(x)/f(x) dx = log|f(x)| is a standard result used throughout this chapter, and ∫1 dx = x closes off the second piece.
common_mistakes: Dropping the modulus bars on the log.
steps.memory_tip: A=1 and B=1 here means the final answer is simply log|Dr| + x — no extra coefficients to carry.
